examples.en: My father wears long sideburns.
My sideburns are long, so I need to go to the barber.
That actor's sideburns look cool.
The sideburns run from in front of the ear down to the chin.
Now that you've grown sideburns too, you look different.

examples.ko: 구레나룻에 흰 털이 조금 섞여 있어요.
examples.en: There are a few white hairs mixed into the sideburns.

explain: 귀 밑에서 턱까지 이어서 난 수염을 말해요. 입 위의 '콧수염', 턱에 난 '턱수염'과 구별해서 써요. 발음은 [구레나룯]이에요.
explain_en: This is the beard growing from below the ears down to the chin. Keep it separate from '콧수염' (mustache) and '턱수염' (chin beard). It is pronounced [구레나룯].

examples.en: Grandpa's back is bent, so he uses a cane.

examples.ko: 꾸부정한 자세로 오래 앉아 있으면 허리가 아파요.
examples.en: If you sit for long in a hunched posture, your back hurts.
He walks stooped over, so I worry about his health.
Your shoulders are hunched, so try straightening them.

examples.ko: 키 큰 학생이 꾸부정하게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The tall student was standing with a stoop.
His back has become hunched as he got older.

explain: 허리, 어깨, 등처럼 몸이 앞으로 약간 굽은 모양을 말해요. 자세가 좋지 않다는 느낌이 있어서 '쭉 펴세요'와 자주 같이 나와요. '구부정하다'와 같은 말인데 더 센 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes the body, such as the back or shoulders, bending slightly forward. It carries a feeling of poor posture, so it often appears with phrases like '쭉 펴세요' (straighten up). It is the same word as '구부정하다' but sounds stronger.

examples.ko: 매일 신은 운동화 뒤축이 한쪽만 닳았어요.
examples.en: The heel of the sneakers I wear every day is worn down on one side only.
The heels of my shoes were worn down, so I went to get them repaired.
There's a hole in the heel of my sock.

examples.ko: 신발 뒤축을 구겨 신으면 발이 아파요.
examples.en: If you wear shoes with the heel folded down, your feet hurt.

examples.ko: 새 신발이라 뒤축이 발에 쓸려서 아파요.
examples.en: They're new shoes, so the back rubs against my foot and hurts.

examples.ko: 뒤축이 단단한 신발은 발을 잘 잡아 줘요.
examples.en: Shoes with a firm heel counter hold your foot well.

explain: 신발이나 양말의 뒤쪽 부분을 말해요. 땅에 닿는 높은 부분은 '굽'이나 '뒷굽'이라고 하고, 발 자체의 뒤쪽은 보통 '뒤꿈치'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the back part of a shoe or sock. The raised part that touches the ground is called 굽 or 뒷굽, and the back of the foot itself is usually called 뒤꿈치.

examples.en: My younger sibling has buck teeth and is getting braces.
Her buck teeth show a little when she smiles.
I worried about my buck teeth when I was little.
I had my buck teeth fixed at a dentist's office in a big hospital.
They say that actor's buck teeth are his charm.
The child with buck teeth smiled broadly.

explain: 앞니가 바깥쪽으로 튀어나온 이를 말해요. 놀리는 말처럼 들릴 수 있어서 상대방 앞에서는 조심해서 써야 해요. '덧니'는 이가 겹쳐서 하나 더 난 것이라서 서로 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to front teeth that stick out. It can sound like teasing, so be careful using it in front of someone. '덧니' is different: it means an extra tooth growing out of line.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 약골이라서 감기를 자주 앓았어요.
examples.en: I've been frail since I was little, so I often caught colds.

examples.ko: 그렇게 약골처럼 굴지 말고 운동 좀 해요.
examples.en: Stop acting like such a weakling and get some exercise.
My older brother was frail, but he built up his body through exercise.
I thought he was a weakling, but he finished the marathon.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에서 약골 소리를 듣던 막내가 오늘 이겼어요.
examples.en: The youngest, who was called a weakling on our team, won today.
He may look frail, but he's surprisingly strong.

explain: 몸이 약한 사람을 가리키는 말인데, 놀리는 말투나 친한 사이의 농담으로 자주 써요. 면전에서 남에게 말하면 기분 나빠할 수 있어서 조심해야 해요. 중립적으로 말할 때는 '몸이 약한 편이다', '허약 체질이다'를 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a physically weak person and is often used as teasing or a joke between close friends. Saying it to someone's face can upset them, so be careful. For a neutral way to say it, use '몸이 약한 편이다' or '허약 체질이다'.
